name: Meshillemith
overview: Meshillemith was a male Levite known primarily as the son of Immer, situating him within the priestly tribe of Levi. His identity is grounded in this lineage, which is significant for understanding his role and heritage within Israel's religious community. Beyond this, no additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Meshillemith means "restitution" or possibly "restitutions" in the plural form, indicating a theme of restoration or compensation. A variant of his name, Meshillemoth, also means "restitution," reflecting a consistent meaning across biblical references.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Meshillemith as the son of Immer. There is an inferred relationship to Meshullam as his father and to Ahzai as an ancestor, though these are not directly stated. No other family relationships are recorded beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Meshillemith's significance lies in his connection to the Levitical lineage, specifically as a descendant of Immer, which associates him with the priestly duties and religious functions in Israel. His mention in 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah underscores the importance of genealogical records in preserving the heritage and responsibilities of the Levites. While not a prominent figure in narrative events, his inclusion highlights the continuity of God's covenant people through faithful descendants.
